sources.title: BnF catalogue: The treasure of Childeric at Tournai
sources.note: Collection history: discovery in 1653, theft in 1831 and recovery of only some objects from the Seine.

sources.title: Ernest Babelon: Cabinet des medailles visitor guide (1924)
sources.note: Printed p. 171, figure 63: electrotype facsimile of the king’s ring; original stolen and melted in 1831; inscription CHILDIRICI REGIS.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Electrum Signet Ring, 17.191.93
sources.note: Seventh-century northern French ring; monogram, material and curatorial discussion of personal seals. No proposed decoding is used.

sources.title: Jean Sorabella / Metropolitan Museum of Art: Carolingian Art
sources.note: Opening and patronage sections: accession 768, imperial coronation 800, learning and script reform. Ninth-century objects are not presented as Merovingian.

scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.
Shared narrative connects imported Franks 400-600 and Frankish Kingdom 600-800 intervals without merging their polygons. Neither represents a precise historical lifetime.
Later features include labels Neustria and Vasconia; this broad imported grouping does not establish uniform Frankish control or certify exact borders.
Clovis baptism remains undated because the sources and modern interpretations disagree.

Pontarlier is a particular estate settlement, not every Frankish home. Building functions, elite status and founding-family graves are qualified interpretations. Published web and annual summaries differ in occupation wording; explicit sixth/seventh-century annual-report dating is used.
No specific toilet arrangement established by the cited settlement summaries. Absence from a summary is not absence in the past.
Medical paragraphs are limited to the verified abstract of Palmer’s manuscript study; no unexamined treatment details or efficacy claims.
Writing sample is Latin on a documented lost fifth-century ring, not a vernacular Frankish sentence or a surviving original.
The former four-passage card’s accepted hash must become stale; this replacement is source checked pending independent review.
No successor links added: dynasty transitions are explained in prose, while map geometry is not independently certified.

proposedOverrides.name: Frankish Kingdom
proposedOverrides.summary: This map interval includes later Merovingian rule and the first Carolingian kings. Farms, crafts and manuscript learning continued across the dynastic change of 751. Charlemagne’s imperial coronation in 800 begins the next mapped phase of a longer Frankish history.

proposedOverrides.name: Franks
proposedOverrides.summary: Frankish rulers built kingdoms within the former Roman world. Clovis expanded his power in Gaul; communities combined older Roman practices with changing institutions and crafts. The years 400-600 are this map record’s coverage, not the beginning and end of the Frankish people.
